items.snippet: AI’s progress in mathematics has suddenly become headline news. In September, Op...
items.raw_snippet: AI’s progress in mathematics has suddenly become headline news. In September, OpenAI announced a proposed solution to the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, accompanied by a proof formalized in Lean. It followed this with 700+ new results spanning almost all fields of mathematical research. This pace of progress is made possible thanks to the verifiability of mathematics. [...] We watch these breakthroughs closely. When AI develops a powerful new capability, we ask what it could unlock for our customers. In this case, the opportunity is to bring mathematical proof into contracts: to show not only what a document says, but why a conclusion follows its terms. [...] Our analysis of Anthropic’s S-1 is an example of our research into Contract Intelligence: using AI to move from retrieval to legal reasoning, from individual provisions to a model of how the whole structure works. The S-1 is a high-profile example, but the same questions arise across companies, partnerships, charities and associations - wherever governing documents distribute rights, responsibilities and decision-making powers.

An AI agent could review invoices, reconcile records, update CRM data, generate reports, and coordinate actions across multiple business systems. Our demonstrations made these workflows look almost effortless.

Investors loved the market opportunity.

Enterprise software was expensive, operational teams were overwhelmed, and executives were desperate to understand whether generative AI could reduce labor costs.

Our CEO, Nathan, understood that demand better than anyone. [...] I asked whether the tracking was broken.

Maya said she’d checked the raw event logs, database records, and workflow execution history. The numbers were real.

Across the room, our CEO raised a glass.

“To the future of enterprise automation.”

Maya closed her laptop.

“Apparently the future hasn’t logged in.”

## The Startup Everyone Wanted to Invest In

Our company, Atlas AI, had been founded eighteen months earlier. [...] [](

Listen

Share

Our Head of Sales was discussing a pipeline worth $18 million, and our VP of Product was telling a journalist that customers were becoming dependent on our platform.

We started with our AI Order Agent, now rolled out across our customer base, which lets buyers submit orders from any source in any format. It's the first piece of a much bigger agentic ecosystem we’re building, and we're moving most of our engineering effort to AI-first work to build it.

You'll own the architecture and technical direction of our AI product suite, partnering with our Director of AI Engineering, including: [...] We're growing and profitable, with 5/5 stars on Glassdoor. Our investors include Felicis Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Poseidon Asset Management, and Village Global, who have funded companies such as Shopify, Cruise, HelloFresh, Facebook, Slack, and Opendoor.

Get to know the team, our culture and our full benefits at distru.com/careers!

The Role [...] The Role

AI is at an inflection point for enterprise use, and AI assistants like Claude, Codex, and Grok are seeing record adoption at work. We believe the system of record has never been more valuable for organizing the data AI acts on.
